subject.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic invalid_request_error as format for failover

question: Should every statusless structured `invalid_request_error` advance the configured model fallback chain, or should this recovery be limited to narrower Anthropic-compatible request-rejection shapes?
rationale: The generic rule is consistent with status-bearing 400/422 handling and fixes the reported lost-turn path, but it also reroutes permanent user/configuration errors across providers; repository policy treats fallback and provider routing changes as compatibility-sensitive owner decisions.

options.title: Approve broad parity
options.body: Treat structured statusless invalid requests like equivalent HTTP 400/422 bodies after the existing specific-reason precedence checks.

options.title: Narrow the matcher
options.body: Restrict fallback to Anthropic-compatible payloads or explicitly observed recoverable message families so unrelated invalid requests remain terminal.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep current terminal behavior until the failover contract and documentation define which format failures may cross model boundaries.

recommendation.title: Approve broad parity
recommendation.body: Treat structured statusless invalid requests like equivalent HTTP 400/422 bodies after the existing specific-reason precedence checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unified failover classifier and adjacent model-fallback architecture trace most directly to this owner’s merged history.
